# Stop Biting
> An app that uses on-device AI (MediaPipe/WebAssembly) to detect nail biting (onychophagia) in real-time via webcam, then sounds an alarm. No camera data is sent anywhere while it runs. Available as a web app (PWA) that runs in any modern browser on a Mac or Windows computer with a webcam.

Every link below carries the page's own description, generated from the same source the page renders — see scripts/sync-seo.mjs. Stop Biting is a paid product and this site exists to sell it; the pages that compare it head-to-head with a competing app say so in their own opening paragraph. One person writes the site: Igor Gazivoda, a software developer, not a clinician.

Pricing:

- Free trial: 3 days, no credit card required — the full detector, streak tracking and incident history
- Monthly: $2.99/month
- Yearly: $29.00/year — about $2.42/month, 19% less than paying monthly
- Every plan includes unlimited AI detection, streak and habit tracking, full incident history, and all alert types (sound and visual)
- Payment is taken through Paddle, and a plan can be cancelled at any time

Key facts:

- Stop Biting runs MediaPipe models in WebAssembly on your own device — once the detection models have downloaded nothing carrying camera data is sent while it watches, which anyone can verify in a browser network monitor
- Detection runs on your device. No camera data is sent while it runs
- It detects nail biting using two MediaPipe models: a hand landmark model tracking 21 keypoints, and a face mesh tracking 478 facial landmarks
- Supported platforms: any modern browser with a webcam, as a no-install PWA, on Mac or Windows
- It detects nail biting only. Competing apps cover more behaviours, run on phones, or cost less, and the comparison pages below say where each of them beats us
- Nail biting (onychophagia) is estimated at 20–30% of the general population and up to 45% of children between age 10 and puberty (Lee & Lipner, Int J Environ Res Public Health, 2022). Both are review-level estimates inherited from earlier reviews rather than measurements, and single studies that measured it directly run lower and vary by population, so treat them as a range rather than a rate
- Habit Reversal Training is the best-studied treatment, which is not the same as having beaten every alternative: its only comparator in the landmark trial was negative practice, and it has never been tested against physical barriers at all. In that trial, participants' own daily episode counts fell by roughly 99% over five months, against about 60% for negative practice (Azrin, Nunn & Frantz, 1980). Five months is the study's duration, not a follow-up after treatment ended, and the counts were self-recorded by unblinded participants rather than measured by anyone else; the paper has no PubMed abstract and is paywalled, so those figures are quoted from Table 1 of the open-access Lee & Lipner review
- The durability evidence is a different trial: Twohig et al. (2003), placebo-controlled, in which nail length was 22% above baseline immediately after treatment and still 19% above baseline five months later, against 3% and 0% for placebo. The meta-analysis of 18 habit reversal studies covering 575 participants reports a large pooled effect, d = 0.80, but from pre-treatment to final post-treatment assessment, and pooled across six classes of repetitive behaviour rather than nail biting alone (Bate et al., Clinical Psychology Review, 2011)
- The DSM-5 classifies nail biting under "Other Specified Obsessive-Compulsive and Related Disorder" only when it reaches clinical severity; the vast majority of people who bite their nails would not meet the criteria for any disorder
- Competitor details are re-verified against each vendor's own website — and against the app store listing that site links to, when the two disagree — and every comparison page closes with a dated "How we verified this page" section stating when the check ran. Read the date on the page rather than trusting a date in this file

## Blog articles

### Psychology

- [Why Do People Bite Their Nails, and Why Is It So Hard to Stop?](https://stopbiting.today/blog/why-do-people-bite-their-nails): Reviews estimate 20–30% of adults bite their nails, and up to 45% of children between 10 and puberty. What drives the habit, and why willpower rarely works.
- [The Stress–Nail Biting Connection: Why Anxiety Drives the Habit and How to Break the Loop](https://stopbiting.today/blog/stress-and-nail-biting): In 339 medical students, 65.7% of nail biters reported tension before biting and 42% pleasure after: self-report, not measured relief. How the loop works.
- [Nail Biting and Anxiety: Is Anxiety Your Driver, and Does Treating It Help?](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-anxiety-treatment): In 339 medical students, anxiety disorder was diagnosed in 22.5% of those with lifetime nail biting against 26.2% of those without. Is anxiety your driver?
- [Why Nail Biting Persists into Adulthood, and What Makes It Different to Childhood Habits](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-adults-why-persists): In a survey of 4,335 college students, body-focused repetitive behaviours tended to be chronic, lasting over a year. Why adult nail biting is harder to shift.
- [Nail Biting and ADHD: Why the Habit Is Harder to Stop, and What Actually Helps](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-adhd): In a psychiatrically referred sample of nail-biting children, 74.6% also had ADHD, the most common co-occurring diagnosis. Why the habit resists and what helps.
- [Why Nail Biting Feels Calming: The Emotional Regulation Mechanism Explained](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-emotional-regulation): Why nail biting feels calming: the reinforcement loop, why regulation strategies often fail to replace it, and how to match a replacement to the mechanism.
- [The Social Cost of Nail Biting: How Stopping Changes More Than Just Your Nails](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-social-confidence): In 3,475 Turkish students, quality-of-life scores were lower in those with nail biting than in those without. The social cost, and what changes when you stop.
- [Nail Biting in Teenagers: What the Evidence Actually Shows](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-teenagers): No source we could find locates a peak age. In a Turkish survey of 3,475 students, 29.2% of high schoolers and 17.6% of university students bit their nails.
- [Nail Biting and Perfectionism: What the Evidence Actually Shows](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-and-perfectionism): The perfectionism link rests on one study of 24 people that used no perfectionism scale: boredom and frustration raised urges, and a stress induction did not.
- [Nail Biting While Gaming: Why It Happens and How to Stop](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-gaming): In a randomised experiment, 40 undergraduate nail biters bit most when left alone and when working maths problems. Gaming supplies both boredom and frustration.
- [What Your Nail Biting Says About Your Personality](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-personality): Nail biting correlates with perfectionism, anxiety sensitivity and sensation seeking, but the perfectionism link rests on one study of 24 people. What holds up.
- [Why Do You Bite Your Nails in the Evening? What Is and Is Not Known](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-evening): No study has measured when nail biting peaks. What has been measured: boredom and frustration brought the most biting in 40 undergraduates.
- [Men and Nail Biting: Why It's Underreported and What Actually Helps](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-men): No reliable sex difference has been shown: 28% of boys vs 26% of girls in 1,131 twin pairs, 20.1% vs 24.4% in 743 schoolchildren. Neither gap was significant.
- [How Phones and Screens Make Nail Biting Worse, and What to Do](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-screen-time): Screen time and nail biting have not been studied together in large-scale research. 15 Android users logged 63.5 notifications a day: scale, not prevalence.
- [Nail Biting and Depression: Is There a Connection?](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-and-depression): In 603 adults with OCD, the 52 who also bit their nails had depressive scores no different from those who did not. What the link is, and what actually helps.
- [How Severe Is Your Nail Biting? A Self-Assessment](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-quiz): A short nail biting self-assessment covering frequency, damage and triggers, with our own rough score bands. Not validated and not a diagnosis.
- [Nail Biting During Exams: Why Stress Season Makes It Worse](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-during-exams): In four conditions, 40 undergraduate biters bit most when left alone and on maths problems: better evidenced triggers than stress. Exam-week tactics.
- [Why 'Stop Biting My Nails' Resolutions Fail, and What Works Instead](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-new-years-resolution): In 339 medical students, 92.2% of nail biters described their own behaviour as automatic, which is why willpower resolutions fail. What to do instead.
- [Nail Biting in College: Why Dorm Life Makes It Worse](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-college-students): Prevalence data show no college peak: 17.6% of university students against 29.2% of high schoolers in a 3,475-student Turkish survey. What changes on campus.
- [Why Nail Biting Increases After Quitting Smoking](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-after-quitting-smoking): We have not found a study tracking nail biting before and after quitting smoking. 40 undergraduate biters bit most when left alone: the gap a cigarette filled.
- [Nail Biting Before Public Speaking: Why Performance Anxiety Triggers It](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-public-speaking): In 24 people with a BFRB and 23 controls, urges rose under boredom and frustration but not stress. The better-supported reading is the waiting, not the nerves.
- [Does Caffeine Make Nail Biting Worse?](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-caffeine): Nobody has studied caffeine and nail biting together, and the arousal premise is shaky: a stress induction failed to raise urges where boredom did.
- [Nail Biting and Alcohol: Why Drinking Can Increase the Habit](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-alcohol): In 339 medical students, 92.2% of biters called the habit automatic. Alcohol dampens the oversight that might catch it, but we found no study on the pair.
- [How to Help a Partner or Friend Who Bites Their Nails (Without Nagging)](https://stopbiting.today/blog/how-to-help-someone-who-bites-their-nails): In the only experiment we found, 40 undergraduate biters bit least when watched in conversation or reprimanded. That is suppression, not change. What helps.
- [Nail Biting in Women: Patterns, Pressures, and What Helps](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-women): No reliable sex difference has been shown: a twin study found biting by age 12 in 28% of boys and 26% of girls. What differs is the scrutiny, not the rate.
- [Why You Bite Your Nails More on Flights and While Traveling](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-flights-travel): Airport dead time beats flight nerves on evidence: 40 undergraduate nail biters bit most when left alone, and a mood induction found no increase under stress.
- [Is Nail Biting Contagious Among Friends and Partners?](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-contagious): Family clustering has been measured; social spread has not. Of 743 children, 36.8% of biters had a relative who bit; a twin study put 50% of variance on genes.
- [Nail Biting During Major Life Changes: Job Loss, Moving, Breakups, and Grief](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-major-life-changes): Stress is the weakest-evidenced part of this. In a controlled induction, urges rose under boredom and frustration but not stress; transitions supply waiting.
- [Boredom Biting: Why an Empty Moment Sends Your Hand to Your Mouth](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-boredom): Four conditions: 40 undergraduate biters bit most when bored or frustrated, least in conversation or reprimand. Another study found no higher urges in stress.
- [Is Nail Biting an Oral Fixation? What That Idea Gets Right and Wrong](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-oral-fixation): A survey of 281 pediatric patients put median onset at 5 years, range 1 to 13, mostly well after the proposed oral stage. The oral self-soothing part holds.
- [Ten Nail Biting Myths That Make It Harder to Stop](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-myths): Anxiety disorder was found in 22.5% of lifetime nail biters against 26.2% of non-biters in one 339-student survey. That myth, the 21-day rule, and eight more.
- [Famous Nail Biters: The Habit Is More Common at the Top Than You Think](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-famous-people): The 20–30% figure is inherited from older reviews, not measured. With a clinical threshold, 6% of 1,378 Australian adults met it. Success doesn't end it.
- [Nail Biting at the Gym and During Sports: What Helps and What Backfires](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-gym-sports): Almost nobody bites mid-workout. In 36 trials, one exercise session shifted state anxiety by g = 0.16, which the authors call small. The risk is either side.
- [Why Do I Bite My Nails Without Noticing? The Subconscious Habit Explained](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-subconscious-habit): Most nail biting runs on autopilot, which is why willpower fails. Awareness is the first trained component of habit reversal, and how to build it.
- [Is Nail Biting a Form of Self-Harm?](https://stopbiting.today/blog/is-nail-biting-self-harm): By the usual definitions, no: nail biting is a body-focused repetitive behavior. What the TLC Foundation and a 1,523-person study say about the difference.
- [Is Nail Biting a Mental Disorder? What the Classification Says](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-mental-disorder): Most nail biting is a habit, not a diagnosis. How DSM-5 and ICD-11 treat it, what experts say, and when it counts as a disorder, from four sources.
- [The Urge Before the Bite: What Is a Premonitory Urge?](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-premonitory-urge): No study has measured the premonitory urge in nail biting. What research on skin picking, hair pulling and tics shows about the urge before a habit.
- [Urge Surfing for Nail Biting: What the Evidence Shows](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-urge-surfing): No study has tested urge surfing for nail biting. What smoking, alcohol and urge studies show, and what the nearest nail biting trial tested instead.
- [Shame and Nail Biting: Does Self-Criticism Make It Worse?](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-shame-self-compassion): Shame raised the urge to bite in a small BFRB experiment. What studies say about shame and nail biting, and why no study tests self-compassion for it.
- [If I Stop Biting My Nails, Will I Start Picking My Skin Instead?](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-substitute-habits): No study we found tests whether quitting nail biting leads to skin picking. What research shows on co-occurring habits and what habit reversal studies report.
- [Does Nail Biting Get Worse Before Your Period? What We Know](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-before-period): No study has tested nail biting across the menstrual cycle. Here is what the closest research on hair pulling and related conditions does and does not show.
- [Does Nail Biting Affect Dating and Romantic Relationships?](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-dating-relationships): No study we found asks how dates see bitten nails. BFRB research shows worry about being judged is common and tracks hair-pulling and skin-picking severity.
- [Does Nail Biting Affect Self-Esteem? What Studies Show](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-self-esteem): No study we found shows nail biting lowers self-esteem. Surveys tie BFRBs to lower quality of life, and in one open trial self-esteem rose as the habit eased.

### Treatment

- [Habit Reversal Training for Nail Biting: What It Is and How to Actually Do It](https://stopbiting.today/blog/habit-reversal-training-guide): In the landmark 1980 trial, participants' self-recorded biting episodes fell roughly 99% over five months. What Habit Reversal Training is, and how to do it.
- [Best Remedies to Stop Nail Biting: Every Method Ranked by Evidence](https://stopbiting.today/blog/best-nail-biting-remedies): Every nail biting remedy ranked by evidence: habit reversal first, then bitter polish, mindfulness and AI detection apps, and what each can and cannot do.
- [Stopping Nail Biting for Good: What Relapses Mean and How to Build Lasting Change](https://stopbiting.today/blog/stopping-nail-biting-for-good): New habits took 18 to 254 days to become automatic in Lally's 2010 study, median 66 (not a nail-biting figure). Why lapses happen and what makes change hold.
- [How Long Does It Take to Stop Nail Biting? A Realistic Timeline](https://stopbiting.today/blog/how-long-to-stop-nail-biting): In the one trial with a real follow-up, treated nail length was 22% above baseline at the end and 19% above five months later, against 3% and 0% for placebo.
- [Bitter Nail Polish for Nail Biting: Does It Work? A Review of the Evidence](https://stopbiting.today/blog/bitter-nail-polish-review): In a six-week trial of 80 nail biters, bitter polish had a 26% drop-out rate against 12% for a wristband, but did better among those who kept applying it.
- [How to Stop Nail Biting Fast: The Quickest Methods, Ranked by Evidence](https://stopbiting.today/blog/stop-nail-biting-fast): Nothing stops an established habit in days. What is realistic is frequency starting to fall in week one or two. The quickest approaches, ranked by evidence.
- [Does Hypnotherapy for Nail Biting Work? What the Research Actually Shows](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-hypnosis): Hypnotherapy for nail biting has no large controlled trials, only case reports and uncontrolled series. What that supports, and what has better evidence.
- [What to Do Instead of Biting Your Nails: 12 Evidence-Based Alternatives](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-alternatives): Match the substitute to your trigger and to where you bite. 12 options by stress, focus and boredom biting, with what research does and does not show.
- [Can Acrylic Nails Stop Nail Biting? What Actually Happens When You Get Extensions](https://stopbiting.today/blog/acrylics-to-stop-nail-biting): Possibly: dermatology reviews say manicures can reduce biting in motivated patients, but no controlled trial has tested acrylics. When they help, what to add.
- [Is There a Permanent Cure for Nail Biting? An Honest Look at What the Evidence Shows](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-cure): The one trial with a five-month follow-up held its gains: nail length 22% above baseline at treatment end and 19% at follow-up, against 3% and 0% for placebo.
- [Stop Nail Biting in 30 Days: A Week-by-Week Plan](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-30-day-plan): We found no published data pinning down which weeks of practice give the steepest drop, so 30 days is a review point, not a finish line. The plan, week by week.
- [Fidget Toys for Nail Biting: Which Competing Responses Actually Work](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-fidget-toys): Fidget toys are popular competing responses for nail biting, but most don't work. Here's which ones do, which don't, and why the match matters.
- [How to Stop Nail Biting Before Interviews and High-Pressure Situations](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-interview-anxiety): Nail biting spikes before interviews and presentations. Here's how to manage anxiety-triggered biting in high-stakes situations, including same-day techniques.
- [Tracking Your Nail Biting: Why Data Beats Willpower](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-habit-tracking): Tracking is the foundation of habit reversal, but in both controlled comparisons that tested self-monitoring alone it produced no significant nail-length gain.
- [How to Stop Nail Biting: The Complete Guide (2026)](https://stopbiting.today/blog/how-to-stop-nail-biting): Habit Reversal Training has the strongest evidence: self-recorded biting episodes fell roughly 99% over five months in the 1980 trial. The method, step by step.
- [Can a Night Guard Stop Nail Biting? What Dentists Say](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-night-guard): Night guards are sometimes suggested for nighttime nail biting and grinding. What they actually prevent, their limits for biting, and when they're worth it.
- [CBT for Nail Biting: How Cognitive Behavioral Therapy Helps](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-cognitive-behavioral-therapy): CBT for nail biting targets the thought patterns behind the habit, not just the behaviour. How it differs from Habit Reversal Training and when to use it.
- [What Actually Worked for People Who Quit Nail Biting, According to Online Communities](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-reddit): Across three BFRB self-help techniques, four-week completion ran 53.5% to 68.6%, so sticking with one is hard. Which community advice matches the research.
- [30-Day Nail Biting Challenge: A Day-by-Day Guide](https://stopbiting.today/blog/stop-nail-biting-challenge): The 30-day plan to stop nail biting as one small task a day, with milestones and what to do after a missed day. Our own structure, not a tested protocol.
- [Can a Gel Manicure Stop Nail Biting? What to Expect](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-gel-manicure): Gel deters rather than interrupts: a coating removes the ragged edges that start episodes, but not a bite on contact. No controlled manicure trial exists.
- [What Nail Technicians Wish Clients Knew About Nail Biting](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-nail-technicians): Nail technicians see chronic nail biting constantly. What they typically recommend, what to expect at an appointment, and how to get the most from visits.
- [Can Press-On Nails Stop Nail Biting? A Practical Look](https://stopbiting.today/blog/press-on-nails-to-stop-nail-biting): Press-ons deter the way acrylics do (harder to bite through, different under the teeth) and cost far less. No controlled trial has tested artificial nails.
- [Essential Oils for Nail Biting: Do DIY Bitter Remedies Work?](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-essential-oils): Neem oil can work on the same aversive principle as bitter polish; the difference is durability, since it washes off faster. No study has tested a DIY oil.
- [Magnesium for Nail Biting: Can It Help With Anxiety-Driven Biting?](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-magnesium): No trial has tested magnesium for nail biting. NAC has one: 42 children and adolescents, 5.21 mm of nail gained against 1.18 mm at one month, none at two.
- [Nail Biting Support Groups and Communities: What Helps and What Does Not](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-support-groups): Across three BFRB self-help techniques, four-week completion ran 53.5% to 68.6%, and they worked to the extent people kept using them. Remedy churn is the risk.
- [Mindfulness for Nail Biting: Useful, Oversold, and Frequently Misapplied](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-mindfulness): In 72 nail biters, decoupling beat relaxation on withstanding the urge, at trend level only on symptoms. Aim mindfulness at the habit, not at general stress.
- [Trigger Mapping: Find Out When You Actually Bite Your Nails](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-trigger-mapping): Most people are wrong about when they bite their nails. A two-week trigger map replaces guesswork with data and makes every other intervention more effective.
- [Habit Stacking for Nail Biting: Attaching New Responses to Existing Cues](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-habit-stacking): Habit stacking works well for building new routines, but nail biting needs a specific variant. Here is how to apply it to a habit you are trying to remove.
- [Using an Accountability Partner to Stop Nail Biting](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-accountability-partner): Social support is a formal component of habit reversal training and the one most people skip. Here is how to set it up so it helps rather than irritates.
- [A Nail Care Routine Built for People Who Bite](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-care-routine-for-nail-biters): Fingernails regrow at about 3.47 mm a month, measured in 22 healthy young adults. Smooth beats short, and the skin usually settles before the nails do.
- [How to Choose a Nail Biting Treatment: A Decision Framework](https://stopbiting.today/blog/how-to-choose-nail-biting-treatment): Habit reversal has the best evidence: self-recorded episodes fell roughly 99% over five months in the original trial. This matches methods to your own pattern.
- [The 5 Biggest Mistakes People Make When Trying to Stop Nail Biting](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-mistakes): Most failed attempts at stopping nail biting fail in the same five ways. Here is what they are, why each one feels sensible, and what to do instead.
- [Nail Biting by Situation: What Changes for Children, Musicians, Nurses and Desk Workers](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-by-situation): The method does not change from person to person. What changes is which triggers dominate your day and which tools you are actually able to use.
- [Does Snapping a Rubber Band Stop Nail Biting? What the Trials Tested](https://stopbiting.today/blog/rubber-band-snap-nail-biting): No trial found tested snapping a rubber band for nail biting. What the trials of mild aversion and competing responses did find, and what to try instead.
- [Acceptance and Commitment Therapy for Nail Biting: What the Evidence Covers](https://stopbiting.today/blog/acceptance-commitment-therapy-nail-biting): No trial found tested acceptance and commitment therapy for nail biting. What hair pulling and skin picking trials found, and what that can and cannot tell you.
- [Inositol for Nail Biting: Is There Any Evidence?](https://stopbiting.today/blog/inositol-nail-biting): No trial found tested inositol for nail biting. What the reviews say about inositol in hair pulling and skin picking, and what is supported for nail biting.
- [Online Therapy for Nail Biting: What the Studies Show](https://stopbiting.today/blog/online-therapy-nail-biting): No trial has tested online therapy for nail biting alone. What video habit reversal and an online self-help trial found for BFRBs, and what to ask a provider.
- [Stimulus Control for Nail Biting: Changing What Sets It Off](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-stimulus-control): Stimulus control is first-line for hair pulling and skin picking. What a case report and two trials show, and what no study has tested for nail biting.
- [Does Chewing Gum Stop Nail Biting? What the Evidence Shows](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-chewing-gum): No study has tested chewing gum for nail biting. What gum did for smokers' cravings, why gum chewing shows up in jaw pain studies, and what to try instead.
- [Does Keeping Your Nails Short or Filed Stop Nail Biting?](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-short-nails-trimming): No trial has tested trimming or filing alone for nail biting. What a 2022 review says about nail care, and what trials of wristbands and bitter polish found.
- [Can Vinegar, Hot Sauce or Garlic on Nails Stop Nail Biting?](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-home-remedies): No study has tested vinegar, garlic or hot sauce on nail biting. What bitter-polish trials found, plus the eye and child safety risks of kitchen coatings.
- [Is It Better to Quit Nail Biting Cold Turkey or Gradually?](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-cold-turkey-or-gradual): No study has compared quitting nail biting abruptly or gradually. What a smoking review found (an analogy only) and what nail biting trials tested instead.
- [Can CBD or Cannabis Help With Nail Biting? What Studies Show](https://stopbiting.today/blog/cbd-cannabis-nail-biting): No study has tested CBD or cannabis for nail biting. What a small THC-drug trial found for hair pulling and skin picking, and why it cannot be applied here.

### Health

- [The Real Health Risks of Nail Biting: What Nail Biting Actually Does to Your Body](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-health-risks): Enterobacteriaceae turned up in the saliva of 76% of 25 chronic nail biters against 26.5% of 34 non-biters. What is measured here, and what is only asserted.
- [Nail Biting During Sleep: Does It Happen and What Can You Do?](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-during-sleep): We could not find a study measuring sleep nail biting: no prevalence figure, no sleep-stage data, no waking comparison. How to tell, and what may help.
- [Nail Biting During Pregnancy: What the Real Risks Are and How to Stop](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-pregnancy): Under the nail was the densest bacterial site on the hand in the classic 26-adult survey. What that means in pregnancy, and which dental worries are overstated.
- [How to Grow Your Nails After Nail Biting: Timeline, Care Guide, and What to Expect](https://stopbiting.today/blog/grow-nails-after-nail-biting): Fingernails grow about 3.5mm a month (22 adults), so bitten nails take several months to grow out. What to expect, and what no study has measured.
- [What Lives Under Your Fingernails: The Real Germ Risk of Nail Biting](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-bacteria-parasites): Enterobacteriaceae were found in the saliva of 76% of 25 chronic nail biters against 26.5% of 34 non-biters: a difference in detection, not a traced transfer.
- [Does Nail Biting Weaken Your Immune System?](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-immune-system): No solid evidence that nail biting weakens immunity in a generally healthy person. Enterobacteriaceae in the saliva of 76% of 25 biters, 26.5% of 34 non-biters.
- [Nail Biting and Gut Health: What Swallowing Bacteria Does to Your Microbiome](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-gut-health): Research linking nail biting to microbiome disruption is limited. Measured: yeasts under the nail in 69.0% of subjects, and raised pinworm odds in children.
- [Nail Biting with Braces: Why It's Worse and What to Do](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-braces): In 21 severe nail biters against 21 matched orthodontic patients, root resorption was higher before and after treatment, direction unproven. What to do.
- [Cuticle Damage from Nail Biting: What Happens and How to Repair It](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-cuticle-damage): Cuticle tissue regenerates, but only once biting stops; repair cannot outpace an active habit. Oil and moisturiser are standard; no trial gives a timeline.
- [Nail Biting and Eczema: How the Two Conditions Interact](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-eczema): Eczema around the nails and nail biting can worsen each other in a specific feedback loop. The interaction, and how to manage both together.
- [Nail Biting During Menopause: Why Hormonal Changes Can Trigger It](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-menopause): No study has looked at menopause and nail biting, or measured stress, sleep or mood against biting frequency. The plausible chain, labelled as plausible.
- [Nail Biting Risks for Healthcare Workers: What to Know](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-healthcare-workers): We found no study on nail biting infection risk in any occupation. In healthcare workers, subungual organisms outnumbered surface ones: mean log10 4.9 vs 3.7.
- [Does Nail Biting Cause Permanent Damage? What's Reversible and What Isn't](https://stopbiting.today/blog/does-nail-biting-cause-permanent-damage): Most damage is reversible: the plate regrows about 3.47 mm a month for fingernails. We found no study measuring recovery time, or how often change is permanent.
- [Do People Bite Their Toenails? Yes. Here's What to Know](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-toenails): The standard review says biting usually occurs in the fingernails, as toenails are rarely bitten. A recognised but uncommon variant, with no prevalence figure.
- [Nail Biting for Chefs and Food Service Workers: The Hygiene Stakes](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-chefs-food-service): Some food codes bar artificial nails: a potential pathogen grew from 87% of healthcare workers with acrylics against 43% of controls, not in greater quantity.
- [Nail Biting in Older Adults: A Less-Discussed Pattern](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-seniors-elderly): Nail growth slows with age on thin evidence: one physician measured his own thumbnail for 35 years, 0.123 mm a day at 32, 0.095 at 67. Biting can start late.
- [Can Birth Control Affect Nail Biting?](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-birth-control): Hormonal birth control shifts the hormonal environment behind mood and stress reactivity. Whether and how it might affect nail biting, explained.
- [Why Nail Biting Gets Worse in Winter](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-dry-skin-winter): Cold, dry air worsens the cuticle damage and rough edges that trigger nail biting. This article explains the seasonal pattern and how to manage it.
- [Nail Biting and Fungal Infections: What to Know](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-fungal-infection): Yeasts grew from the subungual space of 69.0% of 26 ordinary adults: colonisation, not infection. Biting breaks the barrier; the next step is unmeasured.
- [Paronychia: The Infection Nail Biters Get Most Often](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-paronychia): Acute paronychia is one of the most common hand infections, and nail biting is a listed risk factor. No rate in biters is published. How to spot and treat it.
- [Nail Biting and Warts: What the Evidence Actually Shows](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-warts): Beta-HPV DNA turned up in 61.1% of 185 fingernail samples, but those are cutaneous types, not wart types, and the authors cannot tell infection from deposition.
- [Nail Biting and Jaw Pain: The TMJ Connection](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-jaw-pain-tmj): In 240 adolescents, nail biting was significantly associated with TMD signs and symptoms (p = 0.001). Cross-sectional, so it cannot show biting came first.
- [Hangnails and Nail Biting: The Trigger Loop Nobody Warns You About](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-hangnails): Hangnails are both a consequence of nail biting and one of its most reliable triggers. Breaking that loop removes a large share of biting episodes.
- [White Spots on Bitten Nails: What They Are and What They Are Not](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-white-spots): White marks are conventionally attributed to matrix trauma, not a calcium or zinc lack. They grow out at about 3.47 mm a month and can't be treated directly.
- [What Deficiency Causes Nail Biting? What the Evidence Says](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-vitamin-deficiency): Can low iron, zinc or magnesium cause nail biting? What the cited studies do and do not establish, and when to discuss symptoms with a clinician.
- [Does Nail Biting Damage Your Teeth? What Has Actually Been Measured](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-teeth-damage): Less is measured than articles claim: one study on root resorption, one disputed on malocclusion, one on jaw signs. What is established and what is not.
- [What Happens If You Swallow Your Fingernails?](https://stopbiting.today/blog/swallowing-fingernails): We found no study of what swallowed nail clippings do. What exists is one gastritis case report and association studies on germs and pinworm.
- [Can You Get Pinworms From Biting Your Nails? What the Studies Show](https://stopbiting.today/blog/pinworm-nail-biting): Studies link nail biting to pinworm in children, but only as an association. What three studies and two reviews found, and what to do if you suspect it.
- [Staph, MRSA and Nail Biting: What the Studies Found](https://stopbiting.today/blog/staph-mrsa-nail-biting): No study measured staph carriage in nail biters. What finger infection cultures, a hospital worker study and a case report show, and when to see a doctor.
- [Can Nail Biting Cause Cancer? What the Studies Show](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-cancer): No study shows nail biting causes cancer. What a case report, a 261-patient nail cancer study and a melanonychia study found, and which signs need a doctor.
- [Dark Line on a Bitten Nail: Habit Mark or Something to Check?](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-dark-line-on-nail): Nail biting can rarely cause a dark band on a nail, but so can melanoma. What case reports and two dermatology reviews say, and when to see a doctor.
- [Ridges and Grooves in Bitten Nails: Habit-Tic, Beau's Lines or Something Else?](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-nail-ridges-grooves): Ridges and grooves are common in bitten nails, but not every groove comes from biting. What a 53-patient series and reviews say, and when to see a doctor.
- [Does Nail Biting Spread Colds, Flu or Norovirus?](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-colds-flu-norovirus): No study links nail biting to colds, flu or norovirus. A cohort of 219 health care workers found no link with COVID-19, but did for nose picking.
- [Why Is My Nail Lifting From the Nail Bed? Biting or Else?](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-onycholysis): Onycholysis has many causes: trauma, psoriasis, fungal infection, medicines. What the nail biting studies say, and why a lifting nail needs a doctor.
- [Can Nail Biting Give You a Cold Sore on Your Finger?](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-herpetic-whitlow): Herpetic whitlow is a herpes infection of the fingertip. What reviews say about how it arises, why it is misdiagnosed, and what no study has measured.
- [Are UV and LED Nail Lamps Safe if You Wear Gel to Stop Biting?](https://stopbiting.today/blog/uv-nail-lamps-safety): Case reports, lamp measurements and cell studies on UV and LED nail lamps, plus acrylate allergy in gel products. Cancer risk is not established; nor is safety.
- [Does biotin help bitten nails, and affect blood tests?](https://stopbiting.today/blog/biotin-bitten-nails): No study has tested biotin in nail biters. Here is what small brittle-nail studies show, and how biotin can skew some blood test results.
- [Is It Harmful to Swallow Nail Polish When You Bite?](https://stopbiting.today/blog/swallowing-nail-polish-biting): No study covers flakes of polish, gel or acrylic swallowed by adult nail biters. Poisoning reports mainly involve liquid remover swallowed by toddlers.
- [Does Hand Cream or Cuticle Oil Help Bitten Nails and Skin?](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-hand-cream-moisturiser): No study we found tests hand cream or cuticle oil on bitten nails. Lab and review evidence on brittle nails and dry skin shows what is, and is not, known.
- [Do Nail Hardeners Work for Bitten or Brittle Nails?](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-nail-hardeners): No trial we found shows nail hardeners help brittle or bitten nails. In lab tests hardened clippings snapped sooner, and formaldehyde types can cause reactions.
- [Can Nail Biting Damage Your Gums? What Dental Studies Show](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-gum-disease): No trial shows nail biting causes gum disease. Case reports describe gum injury, and four small studies found more Enterobacteriaceae in nail biters' mouths.
- [Does Hand Sanitizer or Washing Clean Under Bitten Nails?](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-hand-sanitizer): Scrubbing and gel cut bacteria on hand skin far more than under the nail. Soap plus a nailbrush did best, gel least. No study we found looks at nail biters.

### Clinical

- [Nail Biting and OCD: Understanding the Link Between Nail Biting and Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-ocd-connection): The DSM-5 files clinically severe nail biting under Other Specified Obsessive-Compulsive and Related Disorder: near OCD, not OCD. What that means for treatment.
- [Nail Biting vs Skin Picking: How These Habits Compare and What Works for Each](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-vs-skin-picking): Nail biting and skin picking are both BFRBs with different triggers and treatments. Learn the key differences and which interventions work for each.
- [Nail Biting as Stimming: When the Habit Is Really Sensory Regulation](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-stimming): Adults with clinical-level BFRBs (n=26) reported more sensory sensitivity than subclinical and control groups. Why willpower misses what the biting regulates.
- [Onychophagia: The Medical Term for Nail Biting, Explained](https://stopbiting.today/blog/onychophagia): Onychophagia is the clinical term for chronic nail biting. Its classification, severity spectrum, and when casual biting becomes a treatable condition.
- [Body-Focused Repetitive Behaviors (BFRBs): The Complete Guide](https://stopbiting.today/blog/bfrb-guide): BFRBs are repeated habits such as nail biting, skin picking and hair pulling that damage the body. What they share, and what the evidence says helps.
- [Nail Biting and Autism: Understanding the Sensory Connection](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-autism): Nail biting is more common among autistic people, often serving sensory regulation rather than anxiety. The connection explained, and what support looks like.
- [When to See a Doctor About Nail Biting (And Which Kind)](https://stopbiting.today/blog/when-to-see-a-doctor-for-nail-biting): Most nail biting doesn't need a doctor. The specific signs that do warrant a visit, and whether to see a dermatologist, therapist, or GP first.
- [Nail Biting and Panic Disorder: When Biting Clusters Around Panic Attacks](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-panic-disorder): For some people with panic disorder, nail biting clusters around panic attacks rather than general anxiety. Why the distinction matters, and what helps.
- [Nail Biting and PTSD: Understanding the Hypervigilance Connection](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-ptsd): For some people with PTSD, nail biting is tied to hypervigilance and nervous system dysregulation rather than ordinary stress. The connection, explained.
- [Dermatophagia: When You Bite the Skin, Not the Nail](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-dermatophagia): Dermatophagia is biting the skin around the nails and fingers, often mistaken for nail biting. It has its own risks and strategies. What it is and what helps.
- [Is There Medication for Nail Biting? What the Evidence Says](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-medication): A 2023 evidence map screened 2,618 psychodermatology studies and found exactly two randomised drug trials for nail biting. No drug is FDA-approved for any BFRB.
- [How to Find a Therapist Who Actually Treats Nail Biting](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-finding-a-therapist): The common failure is a therapist treating the biting as an anxiety symptom and working only on that. How to find one who does habit reversal, and what to ask.
- [Nail and Cuticle Picking (Onychotillomania): What It Is and What Helps](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-and-cuticle-picking): Nail picking is a body-focused repetitive behavior, like nail biting. What the main clinical review says helps, and where the evidence runs out.
- [Is Nail Biting a Tic? Nail Biting vs Tics and Tourette Syndrome](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-vs-tics-tourette): Nail biting is a body-focused repetitive behaviour, not a tic, though the two can overlap. In 535 children with Tourette syndrome, 56.6% bit their nails.

### Science

- [Why Habits Are So Hard to Break, and What That Means for Nail Biting](https://stopbiting.today/blog/breaking-any-habit-science): Lally's 2010 study: the 39 whose data fitted the model took a median 66 days to reach 95% of the automaticity plateau, range 18 to 254. Why nail biting differs.
- [Is Nail Biting Genetic? What the Research Says About Hereditary Habit Risk](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-genetics): In 1,131 pairs of 12-year-old Japanese twins, 50% of the variance in nail biting was attributed to genes. What that does and doesn't mean for quitting.
- [NAC for Nail Biting: What N-Acetylcysteine Can and Can't Do](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nac-nail-biting): In a trial of 42 children and adolescents, NAC at 800mg/day significantly increased nail length at one month but not at two. What NAC can and can't do here.
- [Nail Biting Statistics: How Common Is It, Really? (2026 Data)](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-statistics): Reviews estimate 20–30% of adults and up to 45% of children aged 10 to puberty bite their nails. Prevalence, co-occurrence and treatment figures, and limits.
- [Nail Biting and Cortisol: The Stress Hormone Connection Explained](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-cortisol): No study we found has measured cortisol and nail biting together. What cortisol does, why relief is short-lived, and why stress management alone is not enough.
- [Does Nail Biting Affect Your Fingerprints?](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-fingerprints): Usually not: ridges are set in the dermis and regrow after surface wear, so ordinary biting leaves them intact. Only deep fingertip damage could alter them.
- [Is Nail Biting a Grooming Behavior? An Evolutionary View](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-evolutionary-psychology): Self-directed grooming is described across mammals, but none of that literature studied human nail biting. Read this as an interpretive frame, not as evidence.
- [Nail Biting and Dopamine: Why the Habit Rewards Itself](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-dopamine): Nail biting persists because it is reinforced, not because you lack discipline. Here is how the brain reward system keeps the habit alive, and what that means.
- [Which Fingers Do Nail Biters Bite Most, and Why It Is Not Random](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-which-fingers): Nobody appears to have published which fingers get bitten most, so this is report, not ranking. Your own distribution is still a record of your triggers.
- [Does Nail Biting Come Back After You Stop? What Studies Show](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-relapse): No study we found measures how often nail biting returns after quitting. In one small trial, habit reversal gains mostly held at 5 months. What else exists.
- [Does Vaping or Nicotine Make Nail Biting Worse? The Evidence](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-vaping-nicotine): No study we found looks at vaping and nail biting. One student survey linked smoking with biting, an older one found no link. What that can and cannot say.
- [Does Lack of Sleep Make Nail Biting Worse? What Research Shows](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-lack-of-sleep): No study we found tests whether a bad night makes adults bite more. Child and hair-pulling studies link poor sleep with these habits, but cannot show cause.
- [Does Exercise Help Nail Biting? What Research Shows](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-exercise): No study we found tests exercise for nail biting. Trials link exercise with lower anxiety in diagnosed groups; whether that carries over to biting is untested.

### Comparison

- [Apps and Tools to Stop Nail Biting: What Each Does](https://stopbiting.today/blog/best-apps-to-stop-nail-biting): Compare nail biting apps, bitter polish, wrist sensors and trackers by what they do, where they work and their limits. Includes our own app, with disclosure.
- [Stop Biting vs Mavala Stop: AI Detection vs Bitter Polish (2026)](https://stopbiting.today/blog/stop-biting-vs-mavala-stop): Mavala Stop uses bitter taste to deter nail biting. Stop Biting uses AI to detect it in real-time. An honest comparison: which works for established habits?
- [Nail Biting vs Pen Chewing: Are They the Same Habit?](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-vs-pen-chewing): Pen chewing and nail biting look similar but differ in mechanism and risk. A comparison of the two oral habits, and whether one can replace the other.
- [Nail Biting vs Hair Pulling: How These Two BFRBs Compare](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-vs-hair-pulling): Nail biting and hair pulling (trichotillomania) are both BFRBs but differ in visibility, treatment, and evidence base. A direct comparison of the two.
- [Nail Biting App vs Therapy: Which Is Right for You?](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-app-vs-therapy): Detection apps and professional therapy both treat nail biting, but differ in cost, access, and intensity. This compares them honestly to help you choose.
- [Nail Biting vs Knuckle Cracking: Comparing Two Common Habits](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-knuckle-cracking): Knuckle cracking and nail biting are both repetitive hand habits that work very differently. The mechanisms, risks, and whether one can replace the other.
- [Nail Biting vs Cheek and Lip Biting: Same Family, Different Problems](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-vs-cheek-biting): Cheek and lip biting share drivers with nail biting and frequently substitute for it. The risks and the useful strategies differ in important ways.
- [Nail Biting vs Teeth Grinding: Two Habits, One Jaw](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-vs-teeth-grinding): Nail biting and bruxism share drivers and frequently occur together. Here is how they differ, how they interact, and what that means for treating either.

### Technology

- [How AI Can Help You Stop Biting Your Nails: The Technology Behind Real-Time Detection](https://stopbiting.today/blog/how-ai-can-help-stop-nail-biting): Real-time AI detection solves the awareness problem behind nail biting. Learn how webcam-based AI works, the HRT method it automates, and what to expect.
- [Is It Safe to Use a Webcam App to Stop Nail Biting? Privacy Explained](https://stopbiting.today/blog/webcam-privacy-nail-biting-app): Webcam apps for nail biting raise fair privacy questions. See what data is collected, how on-device AI works, and why no camera data is sent while it runs.
- [How MediaPipe AI Detection Works in Stop Biting: A Technical Explainer](https://stopbiting.today/blog/mediapipe-ai-detection-explained): Stop Biting runs Google's MediaPipe in WebAssembly: a 21-point hand model and a 478-point face mesh, on your device five times a second. The detection stack.
- [Wearable Technology for Nail Biting: Smartwatches and Motion Detection](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-wearable-technology): Wrist-worn wearables are an emerging way to catch nail biting through motion sensing. How smartwatch detection works, and where its limitations lie.
- [How Accurate Is AI Nail Biting Detection? A Straight Answer](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-detection-accuracy): Stop Biting uses fingertip-to-mouth proximity as a proxy for biting. How its settings work, where false alarms and misses occur, and what is unmeasured.
- [Getting Your Camera Setup Right for Nail Biting Detection](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-camera-setup): Detection quality depends more on lighting and camera angle than on hardware. Here is how to set up a webcam so episodes actually get caught.
- [Does Running Nail Biting Detection Slow Down Your Computer?](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-app-battery-performance): Inference runs five times a second, not sixty, roughly a twelvefold cut in compute, at about 640 by 480, with no video uploaded. The cost is real but modest.

### Products

- [Stop Biting App Review: An Honest Walkthrough From the Team That Built It](https://stopbiting.today/blog/stop-biting-app-review): Stop Biting uses on-device AI to catch nail biting in real time. An honest walkthrough from the makers: how it works, who it's for, and what to expect.
- [Products to Stop Nail Biting: A Complete Buyer's Guide](https://stopbiting.today/blog/products-to-stop-nail-biting): From bitter polish to fidget rings to AI apps: a categorised guide to products that stop nail biting, and what's actually worth buying for your pattern.
- [The Real Cost of Nail Biting: What Chronic Biting Costs Over Time](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-cost): Nail biting has a real financial cost: dental repairs, manicures, damaged devices, and more. Adding up what chronic biting actually costs over the years.
- [Can You Use FSA or HSA Funds for Nail Biting Treatment?](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-fsa-hsa): Bitter polish, detection apps, and other nail biting treatments may qualify for FSA or HSA reimbursement. What typically qualifies, and how to check.
- [Do Gloves Stop Nail Biting? An Honest Assessment](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-gloves): Gloves and finger covers are the most-suggested physical barrier for nail biting. They work in specific situations and fail predictably in others.
- [Tape, Plasters and Finger Covers for Nail Biting](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-finger-tape): No study we found has tested finger tape for nail biting. What a 2022 review says about barriers, how tape differs from bitter polish, and how to use it.
- [Does Regular Nail Polish Help You Stop Biting?](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-regular-nail-polish): Ordinary nail polish has no bitter agent and no real barrier, yet many biters report it helps. Here is what is actually going on and how to use it.

### Parenting

- [Nail Biting in Kids: When It's Normal, When to Step In, and What Actually Helps](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-in-children): Clinical reviews estimate up to 45% of children between age 10 and puberty bite their nails. Most grow out of it: how to tell, and what to do if they don't.
- [Nail Biting in Toddlers: What's Normal at Ages 2 to 4](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-toddler): Parents reported nail biting in 23% of 3- to 6-year-olds in a small US interview study: common, not a precise rate. What is typical at 2 to 4, and what helps.
- [From Thumb Sucking to Nail Biting: How One Habit Becomes the Other](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-thumb-sucking): In 1,131 pairs of 12-year-old Japanese twins, finger-sucking and nail biting co-occurred in 17.7% of males and 15.7% of females. Why one habit becomes another.
- [If You Bite Your Nails, Should You Hide It From Your Kids?](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-parents-modeling): In 743 schoolchildren, 36.8% of biters had a family member who bit too, but a twin study put 50% of the variance on genes. Copying is plausible, not proven.
- [Why Punishing a Child for Nail Biting Backfires](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-punishing-children): In a randomised experiment, 40 undergraduate biters bit least in conversation and when reprimanded. That is suppression; punished children learn to hide it.
- [Reward Charts for a Child's Nail Biting: What Evidence Exists](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-reward-chart-children): No study has tested reward charts for children's nail biting. What a pediatric review and a small trial of habit reversal in children say, and what to avoid.

### Productivity

- [Nail Biting During Deep Focus: Why Concentration Triggers the Habit](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-during-focus-and-work): Many people bite their nails during deep focus: coding, writing, reading. Learn the focus-habit loop and how to interrupt it without breaking flow.
- [How to Stop Nail Biting at Work and in Meetings: A Practical Professional's Guide](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-at-work-meetings): Nail biting during meetings, video calls, and presentations is hard to control. Why it happens at work and the strategies that actually help professionals.
- [Nail Biting for Musicians: Why It's a Bigger Problem Than for Most](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-musicians): For guitarists, pianists, and other instrumentalists, nail biting directly affects technique and tone. The stakes and practical fixes for musicians.
- [Nail Biting for Teachers: Managing It in Front of a Classroom](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-teachers): Teachers face unique nail biting triggers: constant visibility, classroom stress, little downtime. Practical strategies that suit a teaching schedule.

### Humor

- [You're Biting Your Nails Again. Your Laptop Saw the Whole Thing.](https://stopbiting.today/blog/nail-biting-laptop-working-from-home): A funny, honest look at why working on a laptop turns even calm, rational adults into compulsive nail biters, and how AI detection can finally break the cycle.
